grade_reason: His only statement since January 2025 that touches risk from AI itself says powerful AI models already present real risks to national security; this is a general acknowledgment, and a borderline one. Nothing found on extinction, loss of control, superintelligence, bioweapons, a pause, or talks with China.
notes: 8 web searches ran, none refused; the three pages relied on were downloaded and read directly. Both quotes were checked by program to be exact continuous passages of the page text, with one caveat: the page's HTML uses non-breaking spaces around "It’s" in the second quote, written here as ordinary spaces (the apostrophe is curly, as on the page). Not a signer of the 23 September 2026 letter urging AI talks with China (not on the verified list). No source showed him co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act; search results named only Sen. Sanders on the Senate side, but no official co-sponsor list was opened, so this is absence of evidence. The C level is borderline: the statement is mainly about government readiness and cybersecurity staffing, and a reviewer could reasonably call it D. Older material (2023 hearings on AI risks; a Global Catastrophic Risk bill whose press release mentions AI being abused in ways that may pose catastrophic risk) appears to predate 1 January 2025 and was left out; its date was not checked. Search results with no 2025-2026 date were not used. Hearing remarks and interviews from 2025-2026 were not found by these searches and may exist.
